s3_monitor_help_title: Signed bucket health — no usage quota
s3_monitor_help_body: Phoenix signs a HeadBucket or canary HeadObject/GetObject. Bucket names may include '-' and '_'; '_' always uses path-style addressing. There is no storage-usage check — the S3 API has no cheap size call. Use a dedicated read-only key.

database_monitor_help_title: Least-privilege DB user + fixed health checks
database_monitor_help_body: Pick an engine and a connection string for a dedicated monitor user. Health checks are presets only (connect ping, or fixed SELECT 1 / PING) — no free-form SQL. Use the setup guide and create-user scripts before wiring production credentials.
database_monitor_capacity_warning_title: These checks need extra database privileges
database_monitor_capacity_warning_body: Session-pool and storage checks run fixed server-side queries — you cannot type SQL. A ping-only user is not always enough. Missing grants become a visible capacity check error while primary availability stays UP; the check is never silently skipped. SQL Server session checks need VIEW SERVER STATE; MongoDB session checks need clusterMonitor; Redis needs the +info ACL; PostgreSQL/MySQL storage usually needs Max size (GiB) because the engine cannot see host disk. Instance-wide PostgreSQL storage needs CONNECT on each database or pg_read_all_stats. Open the setup guide and optional grants before enabling these on production.
